messages:
maya: heads-up — Canary after the 2.3.1 merge is showing a perf regression on short sequences. 95th latency up ~18% for gpt-mini on nv4. CI perf test flagged it during the post-merge run.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout 2.3.1 -> production-canary failed: latency_p95 breach (18%). See metrics dashboard: https://dash/redwood/canary/2.3.1

sam: ack. any obvious suspects? last merge touched kernel selection + batching heuristic files, right?

li: I ran a quick profiler on a canary box. Top diff is in attention kernel dispatch — CPU fallback increased for small sequences. Looks like the kernel matcher prefers the fused kernel only for batch sizes >= 4 now.

maya: that matches my local repro. Short sequences (len<=64) used to go through fast-path fused-kernel at batch=1/2. After the change, policy returns "fallback_scalar" for single-request traces.

jen: do we have the bisect started? if it's the kernel selector change we can pin the commit range to the PR that updated heuristics.

sam: starting git bisect now across the last 6 merges. quick note: CI perf test includes a KV-cache warmup step? if not it could be noisy.

ryan: the CI perf job was the noisy one — it didn't prime the KV cache for the short-seq workload. However the canary metric is real (same regression seen in live traffic with low batch occupancy).

li: bisect result: bad commit is 7f4b2d9 — "tune kernel matcher thresholds" from @alex. It changed the selection rule: prefer kernel-X only when batch*seq >= 256. Previously we used kernel-X for seq<=64 irrespective of batch.

maya: thanks. repro snippet I used:
```bash
# repro driver
python tools/perf_driver.py --model gpt-mini --seq 32 --batch 1 --warmup 50 --iter 300 --profile
```
Profiler diff shows:
- fused-kernel time: 4.1ms -> 6.0ms (single thread per GPU)
- scalar fallback time increased from 3.9ms -> 6.2ms (higher overhead + missing vectorized path)

sam: so the matcher change caused more scalar fallbacks at low occupancy. That explains the p95 impact. Two things: revert immediately or ship targeted fix in selector. Revert would be fastest to restore SLA.

jen: revert approved by oncall. open PR to revert 7f4b2d9 and start canary rollback?

deploy-bot: Revert PR opened: #2481 by jen. Triggering canary rollback...

maya: while we revert, we should harden CI to catch this class of regression. Current perf test uses a single random seed and no KV priming. It missed the edge-case because local dev didn't run warm-warm caches.

li: proposal: add a new micro-benchmark to perf-suite: "short-seq low-batch kernel-path" with deterministic workload: seq=32 batch=1, with explicit KV priming pass and 3-trial median aggregation. Also tighten thresholds: p95 delta allowed = 5% absolute, p95 regression fail if >7%.

sam: +1. Also add an assertion in the kernel matcher unit tests to ensure kernel-X is selected for seq<=64 when batch*seq < 256 and optics indicate vectorized path available. That prevents accidental broadening of the threshold.

ryan: note on flaky tests: the perf CI occasionally flips because of noisy infra. To reduce flakiness we should:
- pin CUDA driver minor version in CI images
- increase repetitions and use median-of-3 instead of mean
- require warmup iterations and explicit KV priming step

maya: created perf-signal epic and ticket PERF-512 to add the micro-benchmark and update thresholds. Also created a follow-up to add a canary alert that triggers if the kernel-path distribution shifts >10% from baseline.

jen: rollback completed, canary metrics returning to baseline within 12 minutes. Reopening the selector PR to adjust logic and add unit tests, not to reintroduce the regression.

li: one more gotcha discovered during profiling: the selector change also toggled an unnecessary KV eviction on path X due to a misplaced condition, causing extra memcpy costs in batching. we'll fix that in the updated PR.

sam: action items summarized:
- jen: revert merged and monitor canary (done)
- li: update selector PR with narrower thresholds + unit tests + remove accidental KV eviction (ETA EOD)
- maya: add micro-benchmark to perf-suite + CI configuration changes (ETA 2 days)
- ryan: update CI image to pin CUDA and change aggregation to median-of-3 (ETA 3 days)

maya: thanks all — good catch. filing a short retro note for next all-hands: tighten perf acceptance gates and bake kernel-path checks into presubmit. :memo: :rocket:
